questions.question: are there any hotel or inn in magallanes?
questions.reply:
No hotels, inns or motels are listed in Magallanes itself. Places to stay in town:
• Horizon Bay Resort & Events Place — beachfront resort with staycation rentals, Purok 4, Barangay Santo Niño (0917 717 7985; on Facebook as "Horizon BAY"). The only Magallanes entry on the DOT-accredited accommodation list.
• Centennial Beach Resort — across from the Centennial Bitaug Tree in Caloc-an, with cottages and a small pool for day visits (please check that it is open).

The nearest inns and hotels are in Butuan City, about 7.5 km away (DOT-accredited, 2023 list):
• Wayfarer Pension House — T. Calo Ext., Limaha (0947 998 3604)
• Casa Mia Lodging House — San Ignacio (0919 877 5982)
• Panyers House Bed and Breakfast — Jose Rizal (0927 281 0874)
• Almont Hotel — San Jose St. ((085) 342-5464)
• Hotel Oazis — J.C. Aquino Ave. ((085) 341-9788)
• Go Hotels Butuan — J.C. Aquino Ave. ((085) 341-1570)
Please call ahead to confirm rates and availability.

questions.question: are there prenatal check up?
questions.reply: Prenatal check-ups are available at your barangay, through the barangay health workers (BHWs) and HRH nurses. Laboratory tests are available too. For an ultrasound, the Rural Health Unit refers you to a diagnostic center.

questions.question: asa ang bituag tree?
questions.reply: Ang Philippine Centennial Tree usa ka Bitaug (Calophyllum inophyllum) sa Barangay Caloc-an. Gideklarar kini sa DENR nga Philippine Centennial Tree niadtong 1998; mga 500 ka tuig na kini ug mga 290 cm ang diyametro sa punoan, usa sa pinakakaraan nga kahoy sa nasud. Nabali ang dagkong sanga niini niadtong Hunyo 2017. Daghang aninipot sa palibot inig kagabhion. Maadto kini pinaagi sa tricycle o habal-habal gikan sa Poblacion, ug walay entrance fee.

questions.question: history sa magallanes
questions.reply: Ang Magallanes kaniadto kabahin sa Butuan ug nahimong kaugalingong lungsod niadtong Hunyo 21, 1969 pinaagi sa Republic Act No. 5660. Gikan ang ngalan kang Ferdinand Magellan (Espanyol nga porma sa iyang ngalan), kansang ekspedisyon gituohan nga nagmisa diri niadtong Abril 8, 1521 — ang hitabo nga gimarkahan sa Magellan Shrine sa Poblacion.

questions.question: how can I get to magallanes?
questions.reply: Magallanes is just north of Butuan City (about 7.5 km in a straight line). You can come by road from Butuan, or by boat along the Agusan River (about 45 minutes). The nearest airport is Bancasi Airport in Butuan City; Laguindingan Airport (Cagayan de Oro) is farther. Around town, tricycles serve the Poblacion and nearby barangays, and habal-habal reaches the upland barangays.

questions.question: how do I report child abuse?
questions.reply:
If a child is in danger now, call 911 or the PNP at 0947 994 4405. To report abuse, neglect, exploitation or child labor (RA 7610), go to:
• the MSWDO at the Municipal Hall, whose social workers handle child protection cases;
• the PNP's Women and Children Protection Desk; or
• your Barangay Hall (Barangay Council for the Protection of Children).
You can report without being the child's relative, and your identity is kept confidential.

questions.question: how much is a building permit fee?
questions.reply:
Building permit fees follow the fee schedule of the National Building Code (PD 1096, Revised IRR), so the amount depends on your plans — mainly the use of the building, its floor area, cost and height. The Municipal Engineering Office computes the exact total.

Building fee for a single-family house, per sq. meter of floor area (the whole area is charged at its bracket's rate):
• New construction up to 20 m²: ₱2.00
• Addition/renovation up to 20 m²: ₱2.40
• Above 20 to 50 m²: ₱3.40
• Above 50 to 100 m²: ₱4.80
• Above 100 to 150 m²: ₱6.00
• Above 150 m²: ₱7.20
Example: a 75 m² house pays 75 × ₱4.80 = ₱360.

Other fees are added, for example:
• Line and grade: ₱24.00 for the first 10 m of frontage, plus ₱2.40 per extra meter
• Electrical: ₱200 for a connected load of 5 kVA or less
• Fence of masonry or concrete up to 1.80 m tall: ₱3.00 per meter
• Certificate of Occupancy: ₱100 to ₱800 depending on the computed cost (₱400 for a 75 m² house)
Plumbing and other fees depend on the fixtures and systems in your plans.

questions.question: how to get police clearance?
questions.reply: Police clearances are issued by the PNP through the National Police Clearance System: register and book an appointment online at pnpclearance.ph, pay online or over the counter, then appear at the chosen police station for your photo and fingerprints. Bring two valid IDs. First-time jobseekers can get it free with a barangay certificate (RA 11261). Check the current fee on the site.

questions.question: how to pay real property tax?
questions.reply:
Real property tax (amilyar) is paid at the Municipal Treasurer's Office at the Municipal Hall. Bring your tax declaration or last official receipt.
• When: in full on or before March 31, or in four quarterly installments due March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31 (Local Government Code, Sec. 250).
• How much: a percentage of your property's assessed value — the basic tax (up to 1%) plus 1% for the Special Education Fund. The Treasurer's Office computes it from your tax declaration.
• Discount: the LGU may grant up to 20% for advance or prompt payment by ordinance (Sec. 251) — ask what applies this year.
• Late payment: interest of 2% a month on the unpaid tax, up to 36 months (Sec. 255).

questions.question: how to renew business permit?
questions.reply:
Renewal runs every January, from the first working days of the month until January 20. The Sangguniang Bayan, with the Mayor's approval, usually extends it to January 30. If there is no extension, late renewals are penalized starting January 21.

For renewal, please prepare: (1) Previous Year Business Permit & Official Receipts, (2) Barangay Clearance for Renewal, (3) Income Tax Return (ITR) or Financial Statements, and (4) Updated Sanitary & Fire Inspection Clearances.

questions.question: how to report a concern
questions.reply:
To report a damaged road, flooding, a streetlight outage, a water supply or waste collection problem, or a peace-and-order concern, use the Report a Concern page of this website. You get a reference number right away, and the Public Assistance Desk routes your report to the responsible office within one working day. Include the exact location or a landmark.

For emergencies, don't use the form — call:
• MERT (emergency response and rescue): 0938 759 1508
• BFP (fire): 0931 721 8881
• PNP (police): 0947 994 4405
• National emergency hotline: 911

questions.question: is there a dentist at the RHU
questions.reply: Under the DOH oral health programme, Rural Health Units with a dentist offer basic dental care — check-ups, tooth extraction and fluoride for children — usually free. Ask the Municipal Health Office (Rural Health Unit) whether a dentist is assigned and on which days. For severe pain with swelling or fever, go to a hospital.

questions.question: is there an assistance for fire victim?
questions.reply:
Help with burial, medical and hospital costs, and educational needs is available through DSWD's Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) and the MSWDO. Usual requirements:
• Burial: the death certificate, funeral contract, barangay certificate of indigency, and the applicant's valid ID
• Medical: a medical certificate or clinical abstract, the hospital bill or prescription, barangay certificate of indigency, and a valid ID
Victims of fire, floods and other calamities can also ask the MSWDO for help.
Apply at the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) or the DSWD field office.

questions.question: on what day or days are free vaccination for babies?
questions.reply:
Routine vaccines for babies are free at the Rural Health Unit and the barangay health stations (DOH National Immunization Program). The usual schedule:
• At birth: BCG and hepatitis B
• 6, 10 and 14 weeks: pentavalent, oral polio and pneumococcal (PCV), plus IPV at 14 weeks
• 9 and 12 months: measles-mumps-rubella (MMR)
Bring the baby's immunization card. Ask your barangay health worker or the RHU for the vaccination day in your barangay, and catch up on any missed dose.

questions.question: requirements for birth certificate?
questions.reply:
To register a birth — a newborn's or a late registration — the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) uses one checklist:

LATE REGISTRATION OF BIRTH CERTIFICATE
CHECKLIST OF REQUIREMENTS

1. Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Negative Result
2. National ID (1 yr old and above)
3. 2x2 size picture w/ white background (unedited front-facing photo)
4. Affidavit of Two (2) Disinterested Persons
5. Any two (2) of the following documents evidence which may show the name of the child:
   a. Baptismal Certificate
   b. School Records
   c. Income Tax Return
   d. Medical Records, Immunization record
   e. Voter Registration Record (VRR)
   f. Philhealth (MDR)
6. Valid ID of Informant, Senior Citizen ID
7. Marriage Certificate of document owner, if applicable
8. Siblings birth certificate, if applicable
9. Any two (2) documents evidences showing of the identity of parents:
   a. Certificate of Live Birth of Parents
   b. Government issued ID
   c. Marriage Cert. of Parents
   d. Death Cert. of Parents
10. Barangay Certification as proof of residency
11. Affidavit of Acknowledgment, Affidavit of Admission of Paternity, Affidavit to use the surname of the father, and Certificate of Registration (for illegitimate child), if applicable

If the birth is already registered and you only need a copy of the certificate, ask the LCRO or request a PSA copy.

questions.question: unsay requirements sa birth certificate
questions.reply:
Sa pagparehistro sa birth — bag-ong natawo man o late registration — usa ra ka checklist ang gamiton sa Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO):
1. PSA Negative Result
2. National ID (kung 1 ka tuig pataas)
3. 2x2 nga picture nga puti ang background (dili edited, nag-atubang)
4. Affidavit of Two (2) Disinterested Persons
5. Bisan unsang duha (2) ka dokumento nga nagpakita sa ngalan sa bata (pananglitan: Baptismal Certificate, School Records, ITR, Medical/Immunization Record, Voter Registration Record, PhilHealth MDR)
6. Valid ID sa informant (o Senior Citizen ID)
7. Marriage Certificate sa tag-iya sa dokumento, kung aplikable
8. Birth certificate sa mga igsoon, kung aplikable
9. Bisan unsang duha (2) ka dokumento nga nagpamatuod sa identity sa mga ginikanan
10. Barangay Certification isip pamatuod nga diri ka nagpuyo
11. Para sa illegitimate nga anak, kung aplikable: Affidavit of Acknowledgment/Admission of Paternity, Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father (AUSF), ug Certificate of Registration

Kung narehistro na ang birth ug kopya ra ang imong kinahanglan, pangutana sa LCRO o mangayo og PSA copy.

questions.question: Do I need a permit to build a fence?
questions.reply: Electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fencing and demolition permits are "ancillary" permits under the National Building Code. They are issued by the Office of the Building Official (Municipal Engineering Office) — with the building permit for a new building, or on their own for a fence, a renovation or a demolition. Bring the plans for that work, signed and sealed by a licensed engineer (an electrical engineer for wiring). For a new electric connection, ANECO asks for the Certificate of Final Electrical Inspection (CFEI) from the same office.

questions.question: Do I need a permit to renovate my house?
questions.reply: For a building permit application, you'll need: 5 copies of Building Plans (Architectural/Civil, sign & sealed); 4 copies of Electrical Diagram/Plans (sign & sealed); 5 copies of Bill of Materials for the building with estimate; 4 copies of Bill of Materials for electrical with estimate; 5 copies of a Notarized Building Application Form; 4 copies of Plumbing/Sanitary Plan (sign & sealed); 1 copy of Barangay Clearance Certificate; and 2 pieces of long brown envelopes. You can also ask me about requirements for a two-storey building, lot ownership documents, or the Certificate of Occupancy.

questions.question: Good morning, I would like to ask about the requirements for a new business permit because I am planning to open a small sari-sari store near the public market in Poblacion and I want to make sure I have all the documents ready before going to the municipal hall next week, thank you very much for your help.
questions.reply:
Requirements for a NEW business permit (BPLO checklist):
1. Barangay Business Clearance — from the barangay where your business is located
2. Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)
3. Business registration:
   • DTI — single proprietorship (for example, a sari-sari store)
   • SEC — corporation
   • CDA — cooperative
Local clearances:
4. Block tiendas, public market occupants and water refilling stations: go to the MEEDMO
5. Sanitary Permit / Health Certificate
6. Zoning Clearance
7. Assessor's Clearance
8. Municipal Engineering Office clearance
9. Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) clearance
10. MENRO Certification
You can ask me how much it costs, how long it takes, or where to apply.

questions.question: How do I change the gender entry in my birth certificate?
questions.reply: Correcting the sex (gender) entry in a birth certificate (RA 10172) costs more than a clerical correction — about ₱6,000 — and has more requirements. Please ask the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) for the complete list before you file.

questions.question: How do I file a complaint against an employee?
questions.reply:
You can complain about a public employee's service, conduct or corruption through:
• Hotline 8888 — the national Citizens' Complaint Center (call 8888).
• The Civil Service Commission's Contact Center ng Bayan (contactcenterngbayan.gov.ph), for poor frontline service, fixers and red tape.
• The Office of the Ombudsman (ombudsman.gov.ph), for graft, bribery and misconduct of officials and employees.
You can also write to the head of the office or the Mayor's Office, or use the Report a Concern form on this website. Note the date, office and names, and keep any receipts.

questions.question: How do I get a certificate of good moral character?
questions.reply:
It depends on who asks for it:
• For a job or as a resident — a Barangay Certification of Good Moral Character from your Barangay Hall. Bring a valid ID; the barangay sets the fee.
• For school or a scholarship — usually from your last school's guidance or registrar's office.
If it is for your first job, ask for the first-time jobseeker certification too — it makes your clearances free.

questions.question: How do I get a certified true copy of my tax declaration?
questions.reply: Tax declarations and property assessments are handled by the Municipal Assessor's Office at the Municipal Hall. For a certified copy, bring a valid ID and the property's details (owner's name, location, or tax declaration number); ask the office about the fee. To declare a new building or transfer a tax declaration after a sale, bring the deed or title documents and the BIR Certificate Authorizing Registration.

questions.question: How do I get a copy of my birth certificate?
questions.reply:
There are two kinds of copies:
• Local copy — a certified copy or transcription (Municipal Form 1A for birth, 2A for death, 3A for marriage) from the Local Civil Registry Office, if the event was registered in Magallanes. Bring a valid ID; ask the office about the fee.
• PSA copy — on security paper from the Philippine Statistics Authority, which most passports, visas and employers require. Ask me how to get a PSA copy.

questions.question: How do I get a health certificate for food handlers?
questions.reply:
A health card shows that a business owner or employee is healthy. Everyone working in the business needs one, the owner included.
1. Pass the laboratory tests: sputum and urine (eateries, bakeries and other food businesses also need a stool test).
2. Once your results are okay, the Municipal Health Office issues your health card.
The fee is about ₱275 (₱235 was also mentioned), paid at the Municipal Hall.

questions.question: How do I get a tax declaration for my lot?
questions.reply: Tax declarations and property assessments are handled by the Municipal Assessor's Office at the Municipal Hall. For a certified copy, bring a valid ID and the property's details (owner's name, location, or tax declaration number); ask the office about the fee. To declare a new building or transfer a tax declaration after a sale, bring the deed or title documents and the BIR Certificate Authorizing Registration.

questions.question: How do I get a zoning or locational clearance?
questions.reply: A locational (zoning) clearance confirms that what you plan to build or operate is allowed where your lot is. It comes from the town's zoning administrator — the Municipal Planning and Development Office (MPDO) at the Municipal Hall — and is needed before a building permit. Usually bring the lot's title or tax declaration (or a lease or authority from the owner), a vicinity map or lot plan, and your building plans; ask the MPDO about the fee.

questions.question: How do I register a child born out of wedlock with the father's surname?
questions.reply: To register a death, go to the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) at the Municipal Hall within 30 days. Bring the Certificate of Death (Municipal Form 103), filled out and signed by the attending physician — or, if no doctor attended, examined and signed by the Municipal Health Officer — and a valid ID of the informant. Once the death is registered, the burial permit is issued (Sanitation Code, PD 856); a transfer permit is needed if the burial is in another town. Ask me "how much is a death certificate?" for the fee.

questions.question: How do I request a copy of an ordinance?
questions.reply: Municipal ordinances — including any curfew, liquor or smoking rules — are passed by the Sangguniang Bayan. They are not posted on this website yet. By law (Local Government Code, Sec. 59) each ordinance is posted at the Municipal Hall's bulletin board and in other public places, and you can ask the Sangguniang Bayan office for a copy or request one through FOI. For curfew hours in your area, ask your Barangay Hall or the PNP.

questions.question: How do I transfer a land title to my name?
questions.reply:
A land title transfer goes through national and provincial offices, in this order:
1. BIR — pay the capital gains tax (or estate or donor's tax) and documentary stamp tax, and get the Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR).
2. Transfer tax — paid at the Provincial Treasurer's Office (Local Government Code, Sec. 135).
3. Registry of Deeds — submit the deed, CAR and tax receipts for the new title in your name.
4. Municipal Assessor's Office — have the tax declaration transferred to your name.
The real property tax must be paid up first; the Municipal Treasurer's Office issues the tax clearance.

questions.question: How long does it take to process a business permit?
questions.reply: Processing a business permit typically takes 1 to 3 working days once all required documents, inspections, and clearances are submitted.

questions.question: How much is the rent for a market stall?
questions.reply: Block tiendas, occupants of public spaces such as the public market, and water refilling stations get their clearance from the MEEDMO (Municipal Economic Enterprises Development and Management Office) before applying for the business permit at the BPLO.

questions.question: I am from Butuan, how can I go there?
questions.reply: Magallanes is just north of Butuan City (about 7.5 km in a straight line). You can come by road from Butuan, or by boat along the Agusan River (about 45 minutes). The nearest airport is Bancasi Airport in Butuan City; Laguindingan Airport (Cagayan de Oro) is farther. Around town, tricycles serve the Poblacion and nearby barangays, and habal-habal reaches the upland barangays.

questions.question: I heard there is a 500 year old tree here, where is it?
questions.reply: The Philippine Centennial Tree is a Bitaug (Calophyllum inophyllum) in Barangay Caloc-an. The DENR declared it a Philippine Centennial Tree in 1998; it is estimated at around 500 years old with a trunk about 290 cm in diameter, making it one of the oldest known trees in the country. It lost large branches in June 2017. Fireflies gather in the area at dusk. It is reachable by tricycle or habal-habal from Poblacion, and there is no entrance fee.

questions.question: I want to sell food at the public market, how do I get a stall?
questions.reply: Block tiendas, occupants of public spaces such as the public market, and water refilling stations get their clearance from the MEEDMO (Municipal Economic Enterprises Development and Management Office) before applying for the business permit at the BPLO.

questions.question: Is there a day care center in our barangay?
questions.reply: By law (RA 6972) every barangay should have a day care centre, now called a Child Development Center, run with the MSWDO. They take children aged 3 to 4 for early learning before kindergarten, and the public ones are free. Enroll at the centre in your barangay — usually with the child's birth certificate and immunization record — or ask your Barangay Hall or the MSWDO which centre serves your area.

questions.question: Is there a penalty for late renewal of business permit?
questions.reply: Renewal runs every January, from the first working days of the month until January 20. The Sangguniang Bayan, with the Mayor's approval, usually extends it to January 30. If there is no extension, late renewals are penalized starting January 21. The BPLO at the Municipal Hall can tell you the exact penalty for a late renewal.

questions.question: Is there class suspension today because of the typhoon?
questions.reply: I don't have live weather data. For forecasts and storm signals, check PAGASA (pagasa.dost.gov.ph); for local advisories, evacuations and class suspensions, follow the LGU's Facebook page (facebook.com/MagallanesADNPIO) and the News page of this website. In an emergency, call MERT at 0938 759 1508 or 911.

questions.question: Mali ang spelling sa akong birth certificate, unsaon pag-ayo?
questions.reply: Ang sayop sa birth certificate, sama sa sayop nga spelling sa ngalan, i-correct pinaagi sa Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO), bisan usa ra ka letra ang sayop (RA 9048). Ang bayad kasagaran ₱1,500. Ang LCRO ang mosulti kung unsa nga mga dokumento ang dad-on. Ang pag-correct sa sex (gender) entry lahi nga proseso ug mas mahal.

questions.question: Need ba ug fire safety inspection para sa sari-sari store?
questions.reply: Oo. Kadaghanan sa negosyo kinahanglan og clearance gikan sa Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) sa dili pa ma-release ang business permit — bisan gamay nga sari-sari store. Pipila ra ka klase sa negosyo ang exempted; ang BPLO ang makasulti kung apil ang imoha.

questions.question: The road in our barangay is damaged, where do I report it?
questions.reply:
To report a damaged road, flooding, a streetlight outage, a water supply or waste collection problem, or a peace-and-order concern, use the Report a Concern page of this website. You get a reference number right away, and the Public Assistance Desk routes your report to the responsible office within one working day. Include the exact location or a landmark.

For emergencies, don't use the form — call:
• MERT (emergency response and rescue): 0938 759 1508
• BFP (fire): 0931 721 8881
• PNP (police): 0947 994 4405
• National emergency hotline: 911

questions.question: What permits do I need to open a sari-sari store?
questions.reply:
Requirements for a NEW business permit (BPLO checklist):
1. Barangay Business Clearance — from the barangay where your business is located
2. Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)
3. Business registration:
   • DTI — single proprietorship (for example, a sari-sari store)
   • SEC — corporation
   • CDA — cooperative
Local clearances:
4. Block tiendas, public market occupants and water refilling stations: go to the MEEDMO
5. Sanitary Permit / Health Certificate
6. Zoning Clearance
7. Assessor's Clearance
8. Municipal Engineering Office clearance
9. Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) clearance
10. MENRO Certification
You can ask me how much it costs, how long it takes, or where to apply.

questions.question: Where can a victim of domestic violence go for help?
questions.reply:
If you are in danger now, call 911 or the PNP at 0947 994 4405. Under the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act (RA 9262):
• Your Barangay Hall has a VAW Desk; the Punong Barangay can issue a Barangay Protection Order (BPO) the same day, ordering the abuser to stop and stay away.
• The PNP's Women and Children Protection Desk takes complaints and helps you file a case.
• The MSWDO gives counseling and temporary shelter referrals.
Physical, sexual, psychological and economic abuse are all covered.

questions.question: Where can I get a police clearance in Magallanes?
questions.reply: Police clearances are issued by the PNP through the National Police Clearance System: register and book an appointment online at pnpclearance.ph, pay online or over the counter, then appear at the chosen police station for your photo and fingerprints. Bring two valid IDs. First-time jobseekers can get it free with a barangay certificate (RA 11261). Check the current fee on the site.

questions.question: Where can we walk by the sea in the afternoon?
questions.reply: The Magallanes Bay Walk runs along the Poblacion waterfront where the Agusan River opens into Butuan Bay, within walking distance of the Municipal Hall, the Magellan Shrine and the parish church. It is busiest in the early morning (joggers) and late afternoon, when families gather and the fishing boats come in — the sunset over the bay is the main draw. It is free and open to the public.
